proof.text: The coproduct universal property identifies Y with the categorical coproduct of C a. Mathlib coproduct disjointness and the coproduct open cover show that the ranges of the legs are disjoint and cover Y. For a fixed leg iota a, use the existing localization restriction functor, which is isomorphic to upperStar. This restriction is a right adjoint and preserves products. For b different from a, each section of the restriction of (iota b)_* F b is a section over the empty pullback: disjointness of the ranges proves its underlying scheme empty, and the empty-cover sheaf axiom makes its sections terminal, hence zero. A product with all factors zero except the a-th factor is isomorphic to that factor: use the projection and the map inserting zero off the diagonal, and verify both composites by the product universal property. The counit of restriction left adjoint to (iota a)_* is an isomorphism for an open immersion, and identifies the remaining factor with F a. All these isomorphisms are in ModuleCat-valued sheaves, so no passage through abelian sheaves is necessary.

proof.text: Use the finite ranges of the coproduct legs as strata, their given schemes as domains and their given maps as immersions. Coverage and disjointness come from the coproduct argument. Each range is open and closed. Its intersection with a compact open is closed in that compact open and therefore compact; hence the range is retrocompact and constructible. The stronger constructible scheme-stratification structure in the existing constructibility definition packages these data directly, without a separate finite-locally-closed-stratification structure.

title: Componentwise finite constant sheaves on a finite clopen union are constructible
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, let $Y=\coprod_{a=1}^rY_a$ be a finite disjoint union of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with each $Y_a$ open and closed in $Y$, and let $M_a$ be a finite $\Lambda$-module, with constant sheaves as in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Define a sheaf of $\Lambda_Y$-modules $E$ on the small etale site of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], as a module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] by
$$E(W)=\prod_{a=1}^r\underline{M_a}_{Y_a}(W\times_Y Y_a)$$
for every etale $W\to Y$, with componentwise restrictions and module operations. Then the clopen partition $Y=\coprod_aY_a$, together with the constant finite module restriction $E|_{Y_a}\cong\underline{M_a}_{Y_a}$, is a constructibility stratification [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]; in particular $E$ is constructible as a $\Lambda$-module sheaf in that sense and also in [def-constructible-constructible] for the coefficient category of $\Lambda$-modules.
